battle.title: Side-view battle and combat database parity

checklist.requirement: Side-view battle presentation uses actor BattleCharSet sprites against Enemies and troop placements instead of first-person combat.
Battle records reference Actors, Classes, Skills, Items, Equipment, Enemies, Troops, States, Battle Animations, System, and Terms.
Battle processing commands suspend the map interpreter and resume with victory, defeat, escape, or abort branches.
BattleCharSet, BattleWeapon, Monster, Battle/Backdrop, System2, and animation timing metadata are validated before play.

database.title: RM2K3-like database tabs and minimum field depth

checklist.requirement: Actors include name, class, level range, parameters, equipment slots, initial equipment, learned skills, charset, and battle charset.
Enemies include stats, rewards, drops, monster graphic, actions, and rates; Troops include placements and battle Event pages.
Database tabs cover Actors, Classes, Skills, Items, Equipment, Enemies, Troops, States, Battle Animations, Tilesets, Common Events, System, Terms, Switches, and Variables.
Delete and edit flows provide reference safeguards for Skills, Items, Enemies, Troops, Switches, Variables, resources, and Common Events.

eventPages.title: Event pages, triggers, and command coverage

checklist.requirement: Event pages resolve by deterministic highest-number valid page semantics and reevaluate after commands that affect page conditions.
Each page owns conditions, graphic, trigger, priority, autonomous movement, options, and a structured command list.

Commands cover messages, choices, switches, variables, conditions, loops, labels, waits, transfer, move route, tile change, pictures, audio, common events, battle, shop, inn, game over, and return to title.
Editor affordances include page order, copy and paste, condition pickers, nested command editing, and validation for missing resources.
ChipSet-style map resources slice 16x16 tiles with passability, priority, terrain, lower layer, and upper layer metadata.
CharSet resources slice 24x32 character frames for map actors and events, with transparent-color metadata.
BattleCharSet resources define battle actor frames, while Monster, BattleWeapon, Battle/Backdrop, System2, and Battle Animations remain separate profiles.
Title, Game Over, System, System2, Picture, FaceSet, Music, Sound, BGM, BGS, ME, and SE resources are typed and validated by profile.

runtimePresentation.title: Retro runtime presentation and immutable play state

checklist.requirement: Play mode presents a 320x240 logical surface scaled by the smallest whole-number factor that covers the player shell with nearest-neighbor scaling; editor canvases may remain modern and resizable.
Map runtime composes 16x16 lower and upper tiles, event graphics, pictures, screen effects, menu, save, title, and game-over surfaces.
Runtime overrides, transfer position, variables, switches, battle result, timers, pictures, and audio state live in session or save state, never authoring Project data.
Editor topology keeps lower, upper, and event layers, map tree, chipset palette, database, resources, and play mode as inspectable surfaces.
Project persistence advances to SCHEMA_VERSION = 3 with typed validators for resources, database records, event pages, and runtime-safe references.
Migration and bulk import create a recoverable backup before destructive changes and prove restore behavior after failed validation.
Current v1 and v2 projects either migrate into valid v3 data or fail with actionable validation messages and preserved original data.
Missing Actors, Enemies, Skills, Items, Troops, maps, switches, variables, resources, or command references are rejected at load or import boundaries.
Autorun events block player movement while active and resume input only when their interpreter state reaches a suspension point or completion.
Parallel events run on a deterministic scheduler with per-event wait state, bounded reentrancy, and stable ordering across frames.
Common event calls have recursion limits, clear diagnostics, and explicit suspension behavior for transfer, battle, menu, save, and game over.
Switch, variable, item, actor, timer, and battle-result changes trigger event page reevaluation without mutating authoring data.
Must NOT copy official RTP assets, copied logos, proprietary sample data, exact proprietary dialog layouts, or trademark-confusing names.
